title: String bass versus tubas in Texas and New Orleans
summary: Albert brought Jimmy Johnson's string bass from New Orleans to Texas, where bands used tubas; recalls recruiting him on Annunciation Street in 1929.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What about, we were talking about the string bass, too. You say you had the string bass in Texas. Did they have many string bass players?

Mine was, well, you had this fella that was originally from Louisiana. They called him Manoon. I was living in Houston outside, but he wasn't playing too much. But, I brought Jimmy. He left here with me. And, that was the first time they had ever seen a string bass in a band. It was a novelty to them.
They were looking used to tubas out there.
Right, right. Tubas. Well, you'd see Brent Sparks with, with, with, with, with, with Trank. They had a tuba. Most any band had tubas.
Charlie Dixon was playing too. Charlie Dixon was playing too.
Charlie Dixon was playing tuba and playing trombone.
But, never string bass.
Never string bass.
Yeah, I can't think. I don't know. Maybe, had Kelly had a string bass or something?
Not that I can recall.
If it probably was somebody from New Orleans, if he did.
If he did. Yes, it was, but I don't remember having, having a string bass. He did most, he did most of his singles. He was, most of his work was singles.
Well, anybody, in New Orleans, how many string bass players were there in September of 29? When you left?
Quite a number.
It was common here. Common.

Common things. I see. It just was fortunate that I, I, I was able to get to you now. I don't know how I ever got you now. I remember driving up to his house on Annunciation Street. That's how it was. Someone had recommended him. And he just said, yeah, okay. He picked on up and left.
You don't remember where he lived.
We're up on Annunciation Street.
Way up.
Way uptown.
What about who. Who.
